chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Abu al-Hasan al-Nahdi, raising it (to the Imam), said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), whenever he saw a funeral, said: 'The Praise is for Allah Who did not make me to be from the perished masses'.

key_terms.السَّوَاد: The masses / The general population (literally 'the blackness' referring to the crowd)
key_terms.الْمُخْتَرَم: The perished / The destroyed / Those who have been taken by death

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say when he saw a funeral?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) expresses gratitude for not being among the 'perished masses' (*al-sawad al-mukhtaram*), a term often interpreted in Shia exegesis as referring to the general populace who are overwhelmed by death and the grave's trials. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on *mawt* (death) as a spiritual wakefulness, encouraging believers to distinguish themselves through conscious preparation for the afterlife rather than passive acceptance of worldly transience. The phrase reflects a deep theological distinction between mere biological existence and the conscious, faithful journey toward the Hereafter.
